    //==
    // # IDirectionField2D / IDirectionField3D
    //
    // Fields of unit directions. Evaluation is the generic ValueAt(IField), which
    // already returns the sampled Direction2D / Direction3D, so no interface-
    // specific helper carries weight beyond it.

    //==
    // # IColorField2D / IColorField3D
    //
    // Color fields (procedural textures, gradients, solid textures). Evaluation is
    // the generic ValueAt(IField); no further helper is derivable from Eval alone.

    //==
    // # IComplexField2D
    //
    // A complex-valued planar field. Evaluation is the generic ValueAt(IField);
    // complex-specific analysis needs members Complex does not expose here.

    //==
    // # ITensorField2D / ITensorField3D
    //
    // Matrix-valued fields. Evaluation is the generic ValueAt(IField); tensor
    // invariants are not derivable from the IMatrix surface (see the P3
    // NumericStructures gaps).

    //==
    // # Differentiable field bodies
    //
    // Bodies for the differentiable field interfaces declared in
    // `fields.concepts.plato`: gradient directions, slope, and
    // stationarity for scalar fields, and the divergence / curl classifiers that
    // name local flow behaviour for vector fields.

    //==
    // # IDifferentiableScalarField2D
    //
    // A planar scalar field with an analytic first derivative. The gradient points
    // toward steepest increase; helpers name the directions and critical points.

    // The gradient direction of steepest increase, unit length. Precondition: the
    // gradient is non-zero at the point.
    SteepestAscentDirectionAt(self: IDifferentiableScalarField2D, point: Point2D): Vector2D
        => self.GradientAt(point).Normalize;

    // The direction of steepest decrease, unit length: the negated gradient.
    // Precondition: the gradient is non-zero at the point.
    SteepestDescentDirectionAt(self: IDifferentiableScalarField2D, point: Point2D): Vector2D
        => self.GradientAt(point).Normalize.Negative;

    // The unit outward normal to the level curve through the point: the unit
    // gradient. For an EXACT signed distance field this is the boundary normal.
    // Precondition: the gradient is non-zero at the point.
    BoundaryNormalAt(self: IDifferentiableScalarField2D, point: Point2D): Vector2D
        => self.SteepestAscentDirectionAt(point);

    // The steepness of the field at the point: the gradient's length.
    SlopeAt(self: IDifferentiableScalarField2D, point: Point2D): Number
        => self.GradientAt(point).Magnitude;

    // True where the gradient nearly vanishes (a critical point) within tolerance.
    IsStationaryAt(self: IDifferentiableScalarField2D, point: Point2D, tolerance: Number): Boolean
        => self.GradientAt(point).Magnitude <= tolerance;

    //==
    // # IDifferentiableScalarField3D
    //
    // A spatial scalar field with an analytic first derivative. For a signed
    // distance field the normalized gradient is the outward surface normal.

    // The gradient direction of steepest increase, unit length. Precondition: the
    // gradient is non-zero at the point.
    SteepestAscentDirectionAt(self: IDifferentiableScalarField3D, point: Point3D): Vector3D
        => self.GradientAt(point).Normalize;

    // The direction of steepest decrease, unit length: the negated gradient.
    // Precondition: the gradient is non-zero at the point.
    SteepestDescentDirectionAt(self: IDifferentiableScalarField3D, point: Point3D): Vector3D
        => self.GradientAt(point).Normalize.Negative;

    // The outward surface normal at the point: the unit gradient. The true normal
    // only for an EXACT signed distance field; a field that merely bounds the
    // distance reports a direction that is not it.
    // Precondition: the gradient is non-zero at the point.
    SurfaceNormalAt(self: IDifferentiableScalarField3D, point: Point3D): Vector3D
        => self.SteepestAscentDirectionAt(point);

    // The steepness of the field at the point: the gradient's length.
    SlopeAt(self: IDifferentiableScalarField3D, point: Point3D): Number
        => self.GradientAt(point).Magnitude;

    // True where the gradient nearly vanishes (a critical point) within tolerance.
    IsStationaryAt(self: IDifferentiableScalarField3D, point: Point3D, tolerance: Number): Boolean
        => self.GradientAt(point).Magnitude <= tolerance;

    //==
    // # IDifferentiableVectorField2D
    //
    // A planar vector field with first derivatives: divergence (trace of the
    // Jacobian) and scalar curl. The predicates classify local flow behaviour.

    // True where the field neither expands nor compresses within tolerance
    // (divergence-free / incompressible flow)
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Incompressible_flow).
    IsIncompressibleAt(self: IDifferentiableVectorField2D, point: Point2D, tolerance: Number): Boolean
        => self.DivergenceAt(point).Abs <= tolerance;

    // True where the field spreads outward (positive divergence): a source. Note:
    // near-zero divergence classifies by sign noise; use IsIncompressibleAt for a
    // balanced test.
    IsSourceAt(self: IDifferentiableVectorField2D, point: Point2D): Boolean
        => self.DivergenceAt(point) > 0.0;

    // True where the field converges inward (negative divergence): a sink. Note:
    // near-zero divergence classifies by sign noise; use IsIncompressibleAt for a
    // balanced test.
    IsSinkAt(self: IDifferentiableVectorField2D, point: Point2D): Boolean
        => self.DivergenceAt(point) < 0.0;

    // True where the field has no local rotation within tolerance (irrotational)
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irrotational_flow).
    IsIrrotationalAt(self: IDifferentiableVectorField2D, point: Point2D, tolerance: Number): Boolean
        => self.CurlAt(point).Abs <= tolerance;

    //==
    // # IDifferentiableVectorField3D
    //
    // A spatial vector field with first derivatives: divergence and the curl
    // vector (vorticity). Mirrors the planar classifiers with a vector curl.

    // True where the field neither expands nor compresses within tolerance
    // (divergence-free / incompressible flow).
    IsIncompressibleAt(self: IDifferentiableVectorField3D, point: Point3D, tolerance: Number): Boolean
        => self.DivergenceAt(point).Abs <= tolerance;

    // True where the field spreads outward (positive divergence): a source. Note:
    // near-zero divergence classifies by sign noise; use IsIncompressibleAt for a
    // balanced test.
    IsSourceAt(self: IDifferentiableVectorField3D, point: Point3D): Boolean
        => self.DivergenceAt(point) > 0.0;

    // True where the field converges inward (negative divergence): a sink. Note:
    // near-zero divergence classifies by sign noise; use IsIncompressibleAt for a
    // balanced test.
    IsSinkAt(self: IDifferentiableVectorField3D, point: Point3D): Boolean
        => self.DivergenceAt(point) < 0.0;

    // The strength of local rotation: the length of the curl (vorticity) vector
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vorticity).
    VorticityMagnitudeAt(self: IDifferentiableVectorField3D, point: Point3D): Number
        => self.CurlAt(point).Magnitude;

    // True where the field has no local rotation within tolerance (irrotational).
    IsIrrotationalAt(self: IDifferentiableVectorField3D, point: Point3D, tolerance: Number): Boolean
        => self.CurlAt(point).Magnitude <= tolerance;
